opinions.rationale: The valid core is that a baseline-assignment, treatment-policy analogue permits subsequent initiation, so increasing crossover can reduce exposure separation and may dilute the assignment effect. This is part of that estimand, not confounding bias to be adjusted away. However, crossover also occurs in randomized trials, so it is not uniquely observational. Convergence of current treatment status does not imply convergence of cumulative exposure histories, and attenuation toward the null with longer follow-up is not guaranteed: its direction and magnitude depend on treatment timing, effect dynamics, switching mechanisms, competing events, and the effect scale. A convergence rate alone therefore cannot determine an attenuation factor. Nor does a null estimate become categorically indistinguishable from biological inefficacy; treatment trajectories, alternative sustained or dynamic-strategy estimands, and assumption-based analyses can clarify interpretation, although they cannot identify a decomposition without additional assumptions. Existing target-trial and dynamic-strategy methods substantially address the design problem; context-specific horizon selection and adequate trajectory reporting remain unresolved practice issues. High severity is justified only when the reported estimand is mischaracterized or exposure separation is inadequate for the intended decision.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: In a baseline-initiation treatment-policy analogue that allows later initiation, comparator crossover can reduce separation between treatment histories and, under some treatment-effect and switching mechanisms, attenuate the assignment effect at longer horizons. This is an estimand feature also possible in randomized trials, not a universal bias or a guarantee of movement toward the null.

resolving_work.title: Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Provides the distinction between observational analogues of intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects and the corresponding design and adjustment requirements.

resolving_work.title: Using observational data to emulate a randomized trial of dynamic treatment-switching strategies
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Shows that later initiation and switching can be specified explicitly as dynamic strategies rather than treated as an unaddressable convergence problem.
